chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who married off his slave from a free woman for one hundred dirhams, then sold him before entering upon her. He said, and he said: 'Her master gives her from the price half of what he stipulated for her. Indeed, it is in the position of a debt, if he had borrowed it with the permission of his master.'

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ دَيْنٍ: in the position of a debt
key_terms.نِصْفَ مَا فَرَضَ لَهَا: half of what he stipulated for her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the dowry if a master sells his slave before marrying him to a free woman?
ai.summary: This ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the financial liability of a master who sells a male slave after marrying him to a free woman but before consummation, establishing that the master must pay half the stipulated dowry from the sale proceeds. Shaykh al-Tusi presents this obligation as a debt (*dayn*) incurred with the master's consent, highlighting the principle that the master bears the cost of the 'defect' of non-consummation in the transaction. This case illustrates the nuanced application of *mahr al-mithl* and contractual obligations in Shia jurisprudence regarding mixed-status marriages.
